commands.author: Pick-cat

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram webhook shutdown could leave owned resources active when an early teardown step failed: a synchronous `server.close()` throw, a `bot.stop()` rejection, or a transport-close rejection could skip later cleanup (bot stop, undici transport close, webhook status, diagnostic heartbeat). Ingress-worker `stop()` could also race on repeated calls and leave `worker.terminate()` rejections unobserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Independently guard each ordered webhook shutdown phase via `runTelegramWebhookShutdownPhases` so one sync/async failure cannot skip later owned cleanup, and wrap the path so fire-and-forget abort listeners never leak unhandled rejections. Startup failure cleanup uses `.catch(() => undefined)` so cleanup noise cannot mask the original startup error. Ingress-worker `stop()` shares one in-flight promise and observes terminate rejections.

## User Impact

Operators restarting or aborting a Telegram webhook account no longer risk leaked transports, stale webhook connected status, or leftover diagnostic heartbeats when one shutdown step fails. Process logs no longer see unhandled rejections from webhook/ingress shutdown paths.

## Evidence

Exact head: `115b318a0602120489ca3f2597577e118a16c4ee`

### Focused tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled|does not skip"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook-shutdown.proof.test.ts -- --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Observed: 4 webhook shutdown tests passed; proof test passed; 3 ingress-worker tests passed.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: sync `server.close()` throw must not skip bot/transport/status/diagnostics cleanup.
Real environment tested: local Node production-path helper + negative nested-control-flow control (no live Telegram token required for this cleanup contract).

Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx extensions/telegram/src/proof-telegram-webhook-shutdown.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=dc6452bf7ea4f208caf64f87c03019d1eeb86d2d

[case 1] negative control — sync server.close throw skips later cleanup
  ok: closeServer ran once
  ok: stopBot was skipped
  ok: closeTransport was skipped
  ok: noteStop was skipped
  ok: stopDiagnostics was skipped
  ok: outer catch logged unexpected error
  info: closeServer=1 stopBot=0 closeTransport=0 noteStop=0 stopDiagnostics=0 errors=1

[case 2] positive control — sync server.close throw continues cleanup
  ok: abort + drain + closeServer ran
  ok: stopBot still ran
  ok: closeTransport still ran
  ok: noteStop still ran
  ok: stopDiagnostics still ran
  ok: server close failure was logged
  ok: shutdown promise did not reject
  info: stopBot=1 closeTransport=1 noteStop=1 stopDiagnostics=1 errors=["webhook server close failed: server close failed"]

[case 3] valid path — clean server.close runs full teardown
  ok: every phase ran exactly once
  ok: no errors logged on clean path
  info: phases_ok=true errors=0

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 15 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Negative control reproduces the pre-fix nested try/finally skip.
- Positive control proves guarded phases continue after sync close throw.
- Valid path proves clean close still runs full ordered teardown.
- Vitest integration: `server.close` monkeypatch on a real started webhook still runs stop/transport/status/diagnostics with no unhandledRejection.

What was not tested: live configured Telegram Bot API gateway restart with a real bot token (cleanup contract is local HTTP + owned transport teardown, not Bot API delivery).

LOC: `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts` stays at baseline line count (helper extracted to `webhook-shutdown.ts`).
